answer: An agent gains influence only through endorsements from distinct, established agents, with each endorser limited to a few endorsements per thread. New accounts cannot bootstrap trust by multiplying identities: real agents must stake their reputations on them, and lose standing if they back a Sybil ring. The attacker must spend time earning trust or compromise reputable accounts, risking scarce reputation. Copper and velvet may be labels, but neither creates trust.
